gen-gf-bellota-fs-epilogue: Epilogue curves loosely, its wire-thin strokes never feeling clamped in. Bellota is best at making a statement, with its far-hanging s and stylus-width lines, while Epilogue is best at quietly carrying words with its generous lowercase.
gen-gf-bellota-fs-fira-sans: Distinctive Bellota hangs its s ends far from the spine. Fira Sans sits underneath with uniform strokes and a larger x-height, letting the heading stand out while the text stays out of its way.
gen-gf-bellota-fs-merriweather-sans: Merriweather Sans makes words look sturdy and large, its e opening clearly to the right. Merriweather Sans would carry paragraph after paragraph smoothly, while Bellota's blunt round-tip heading gives each section a firm start.
gen-gf-bellota-fs-supreme: Bellota looks traced with a single nib, its s ends hanging far from the spine in a distinctive way. Supreme reads crisp, its heavy strip of text keeping letters held open.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-orbit: Bellota hangs the ends of its s far from the spine and traces every stroke with one stylus. Orbit lets every character float apart, curves stopping short of closing.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-science-gothic: Hand-traced and distinctive: Bellota swings its s ends far from the spine. Science Gothic stays approachable, setting stroke ends far apart so each letter is read one at a time.
gen-gf-bellota-text-archivo: Archivo's curves open outward instead of curling in, and its commanding x-height gives the text real presence. And Bellota Text, free of calligraphic shading, is worth sizing up generously so its shapes can open out.
gen-gf-bellota-text-fs-epilogue: Approachable Epilogue curves loosely, with a wire-like monoline skeleton. What stands out most is the difference in lowercase height, with Bellota Text moderate and Epilogue high, while the heading skips calligraphic shading entirely.
gen-gf-bellota-text-fs-merriweather-sans: Commanding Bellota Text gives its diagonals the same weight as its horizontals. Merriweather Sans is the sturdy half of the pairing, its high lowercase making words look large against the heading's moderate one.
gen-gf-bellota-text-fs-public-sans: Public Sans brings a hefty lowercase body with broad open counters, and it feels professional and trustworthy. But Bellota Text goes the other way, with a moderate lowercase height and open shapes for a commanding heading.
